The curve shows that the river has relatively large discharge and obvious fluctuations from January to April, very small discharge from May to August, close to a low-water state, and after September the discharge rises again, remaining relatively large from October to December. That is to say, this river has large discharge in the winter half-year of the Northern Hemisphere and small discharge in the summer half-year. Then reason: The question stem states that this river is mainly supplied by precipitation, so the abundance and scarcity of river discharge can approximately reflect the seasonal changes of precipitation. Large discharge in the winter half-year indicates much precipitation in winter, and small discharge in the summer half-year indicates little precipitation in summer, which conforms to the Mediterranean climate characteristic of “winter rain and summer dryness.” Mediterranean climate is mainly distributed on the west coasts of continents at 30°—40° north and south latitudes; in the figure, the low-water period appears in June—August, and the high-water period appears around December—February of the following year, indicating that it is located in the Northern Hemisphere. Therefore, this river is approximately located on the west coast of the continent between 30°—40° north latitude.
